key_terms.definition: One of the three modes by which a man betroths a woman: giving her an object of monetary value while declaring that she is thereby betrothed to him, before witnesses.
key_terms.on_this_daf: The mishnah opens with kesef as the first mode of kiddushin, and the Gemara derives it via a gezerah shavah from Avraham's purchase of Efron's field, explaining why the mishnah uses the language of acquisition (nikneit) rather than betrothal.

key_terms.definition: One of the three modes of kiddushin: a document stating that the woman is betrothed to the man, given to her before witnesses.
key_terms.on_this_daf: Listed by the mishnah as the second mode of betrothal, distinct from the ketubah, which belongs to nisu'in rather than kiddushin.

key_terms.definition: A single act of intercourse performed with explicit intent to create a legal bond (kiddushin, or in the case of a yevamah, the levirate bond), as opposed to intercourse for its own sake.
key_terms.on_this_daf: The mishnah's third mode of betrothal, and the sole means by which a yevamah is acquired by the yavam; the Gemara explains that Proverbs' use of derech for intercourse shapes the mishnah's choice of the word derachim.

key_terms.definition: The first stage of Jewish marriage, created by kesef, shtar or bi'ah, which forbids the woman to all other men and requires a get (or the husband's death) to dissolve, but does not yet establish the shared household obligations of full marriage.
key_terms.on_this_daf: The Gemara explains why the Sages later called this act kiddushin (from hekdesh, consecration) rather than the Torah's own language of kinyan/kicha, reflecting a shift from a pure acquisition model to a status of exclusivity.

key_terms.definition: The second stage of Jewish marriage, effected through chuppah, which brings the couple to live together and creates the mutual obligations of she'er, kesut ve-onah and the husband's right to her earnings.
key_terms.on_this_daf: Distinguished from kiddushin as the outline explains why this mishnah's terse language about the woman's freedom omits the obligations (vows, earnings) that only begin with nisu'in.

key_terms.sense: a childless widow bound to levirate marriage
key_terms.definition: A woman whose husband died without children, who becomes bound to his brother (the yavam) either to be acquired via intercourse (yibum) or released via chalitzah.
key_terms.on_this_daf: The mishnah applies the same in/out framework to the yevamah, who is acquired only through bi'ah and released only through chalitzah or the yavam's death.

key_terms.sense: the ceremony releasing a yevamah from the levirate bond
key_terms.definition: A ritual ceremony that releases a yevamah from her bond to the yavam when he does not wish to perform yibum, freeing her to marry others.
key_terms.on_this_daf: Listed by the mishnah as one of the two ways a yevamah acquires herself, alongside the yavam's death.

key_terms.sense: the minimal coin value sufficient for kiddushin
key_terms.definition: A small copper coin representing the smallest unit of monetary value recognized in halakha, used as the minimum amount for certain transactions.
key_terms.on_this_daf: Beit Hillel set the minimum value for betrothal via kesef at one perutah (against Beit Shammai's dinar), and the mishnah fixes its worth as one-eighth of the Italian issar.
